prompt:
Create one cinematography sheet for shot s01 'arrival and everything at once' of a silent animated film. Four numbered panels in a clean 2-by-2 layout on a pure black sheet; each panel is a 16:9 frame with thin pale outline and generous black gutters. No text anywhere except the four cream panel numbers 1, 2, 3, 4 under the panels.
REFERENCE ROLES. Image 1 is the approved model sheet of the human: keep this exact character (green skin, mauve-and-blue angular poncho, one trailing swoop of cream-and-mauve hair, large hands, flared trousers and boots); do not redesign. Image 2 is the official plate of the two companions: a small blue cloud-headed robot with a dark terminal face showing a cyan prompt glyph (Codex) and a coral rectangular block robot with two dark slit eyes and four small legs (Clawd); keep their identity colours and silhouettes, draw them small. Image 3 is a contact sheet of three COMPOSITION references, for framing only, never copy their subjects or colours: left (a dark scene lit from one side, a small lit group against a large dark mass) feeds PANEL 1; centre (tiny figures dwarfed by a huge lit structure, converging lines) feeds PANEL 2's scale; right (a dense crowded field of many small things everywhere) feeds PANEL 2's density. Image 4 is the HUE card: its blue light fills a volume and figures read as silhouettes inside it; the radiance of this shot is exactly Turrell blue #0a51fb with one scarce accent #fad204 (yellow), nothing else saturated apart from the identity colours of the three characters. Image 5 is a contact sheet of three OBJECT references for the grammar of the pieces only: a single blue cloud on black, swirling wave masses with cream sweeps, strings of beaded lights over dark masses.
STYLE: flat shapes, pale contour, stipple shading only, no gradients, no photographic texture, pure black field; the pieces are Seuss-like swooping towers, stacked pointed arches, ring gates, curling stalks with flag leaves, a beaded light string, kit blocks.
PANEL 1 (upper left) is the POSTER, the first frame of the shot and the START of the camera move: a locked MEDIUM-WIDE shot on black. Left to right: Codex small at the left third, the human standing upright in the centre BEHIND a plain flat box that comes up to the human's hips, the human is about 50 percent of the panel height, Clawd small at the right third. The box is plain and ordinary, the lid closed, with a very thin hairline of blue light leaking at the lid seam, the only light in the frame, at about 50 percent across and 68 percent down. All three look at the box. Nothing else is in the frame.
PANEL 2 (upper right) is the END of the camera move, the full field after the camera has widened: the same three characters are now small in the lower middle of a vast black field, the human is about 30 percent of the panel height, flooded by Turrell blue light from a hybrid machine (stacked blobby lobes, a crooked funnel, a curled antenna with a flag leaf, a round dial) standing close behind the box at about 62 percent across and 52 percent down, which is the single emitter (the dial). From the machine a crowd of pieces fans out along curving lines in every direction and fills the whole field: curling stalks, stacked pointed arches, ring gates, kit blocks, a beaded string, all in blue and pale cream with a few small yellow accents. The human has turned and hunches, small. Codex catches a piece, a stalk pushes Clawd sideways. The frame reads as too much at once.
PANEL 3 (lower left) is a top-down STAGING PLAN drawn in thin pale lines only: marks for the human (circle with a facing arrow), Codex and Clawd (small squares), the box (rectangle), the machine (larger mark behind the box); a camera wedge at the bottom pointing up into the scene with an arrow showing the WIDEN move (the wedge opens wider along the arrow); the LEADING LINE of the move drawn as one swooping curve from the box up through the first curling stalk to the field edge; two small suns marking the emitter positions: the first at the box seam, the second at the machine's dial.
PANEL 4 (lower right) is a SCALE STRIP: the human drawn twice on one shared baseline, left at the PANEL 1 size (about 50 percent of a panel height) and right at the PANEL 2 size (about 30 percent), beside an eight-circle head-unit ruler at the far left, and two round swatches at the far right: the radiance #0a51fb and the accent #fad204.
